# Resolve AMD Instinct hardware access path

## Description

This epic resolves how dedicated AMD Instinct GPU nodes are obtained for the AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement strategy. The strategy's validation work requires physical AMD Instinct hardware, and none exists in the CI fleet today. Two candidate paths exist — direct procurement of nodes into our infrastructure, or access through a partner lab — and the choice is unresolved. This investigation produces the decision and a secured commitment so that environment provisioning and the validation campaign can proceed.

## Scope

- Enumerate and evaluate candidate access paths: direct procurement of AMD Instinct nodes versus partner-lab access (including hybrid options).
- For each path, determine availability of Instinct-class nodes, achievable scale (node/GPU count), lead time relative to the validation campaign's needs, and cost.
- Identify the budget/approval route for procurement or the agreement route for partner-lab access.
- Assess integration implications of each path: connectivity, job submission and results retrieval, security/compliance constraints of remote labs.
- Produce a decision record selecting the access path, with node type and count, timeline, and cost.
- Secure the commitment: an approved procurement or a signed partner-lab agreement.
- If no viable path exists, record the escalation and the implication that the strategy cannot proceed as planned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written decision record identifies the selected access path (procurement or partner lab) with node type, node/GPU count, timeline, and cost.
- The access commitment is secured (procurement approved or partner agreement signed).
- The decided path is verified to satisfy the validation campaign's requirement for dedicated AMD Instinct nodes usable to evaluate the supported model set.
- Any constraints of the chosen path (e.g., remote access only, limited node count) are documented and handed to the validation campaign and environment provisioning work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the validation campaign requires dedicated AMD Instinct nodes; procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved. This epic resolves that open question, which gates all P0 work in the strategy.

# Provision AMD Instinct compute environment

## Description

This epic stands up the AMD GPU compute environment selected by the hardware-access decision, so that validation, serving productization, and training support have physical AMD Instinct hardware to run on. Depending on the decided path, this means either procuring and installing nodes into our infrastructure with the ROCm driver stack and AMD GPU Kubernetes device plugin, or establishing working access to a partner-lab environment with equivalent capability.

## Scope

- Execute the decided access path:
  - Procurement path: purchase, rack, and install AMD Instinct nodes; integrate them into the cluster/CI infrastructure.
  - Partner-lab path: complete lab onboarding, establish connectivity, and validate remote job submission and results retrieval.
- Install and verify the ROCm driver stack on the AMD nodes.
- Deploy the AMD GPU Kubernetes device plugin so `amd.com/gpu` resources are allocatable by the scheduler.
- Verify node/network integration: jobs can be submitted to the AMD nodes and results retrieved.
- Produce a runbook documenting how teams use the environment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AMD Instinct nodes are available with the ROCm driver stack installed and functioning.
- `amd.com/gpu` resources are discoverable and allocatable by the Kubernetes scheduler on the AMD nodes.
- The environment is reachable and usable by the validation and training teams; a runbook exists describing access and usage.
- For a partner-lab path, connectivity is validated end-to-end (job submission, execution on Instinct hardware, results retrieval).
- Environment capacity matches the node type/count committed in the hardware-access decision.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware requires this environment to exist; this epic provisions it.

# vLLM ROCm serving validation campaign (go/no-go)

## Description

This epic runs the validation campaign that establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving on AMD Instinct hardware, across the supported model set, and produces the go/no-go scope for productization. The platform currently ships only CUDA runtime builds and has no first-hand parity data for ROCm; this campaign resolves that unknown. Its outcome determines which models the productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime will support.

## Scope

- Define the test matrix covering the supported model set for vLLM serving on ROCm, using upstream/community ROCm-enabled vLLM builds (productization is out of scope here).
- Run functional validation per model: output correctness against the CUDA baseline within defined tolerances.
- Run performance validation per model: throughput and latency against the CUDA baseline on comparable hardware.
- Record per-model pass/fail results with supporting data.
- Produce the go/no-go report: the list of models cleared for productization, models that failed parity, and the recommended scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every model in the supported model set has recorded functional parity results (pass/fail with tolerances) for vLLM serving on ROCm, executed on physical AMD Instinct hardware.
- Every model in the supported model set has recorded performance parity data (throughput and latency) against the CUDA baseline.
- A go/no-go report lists the models cleared for productization with the supporting data, and explicitly lists models that failed parity.
- The campaign runs on the provisioned AMD Instinct environment.
- The report is delivered to stakeholders for the productization go/no-go decision.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): this epic is the validation campaign — it establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set and produces the go/no-go scope for productization.

# Productize vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by the validation campaign. Today only CUDA (NVIDIA) builds of the vLLM runtime are productized; this epic adds a ROCm build, the serving runtime definitions for the cleared models, and the release integration needed to ship and support it.

## Scope

- Build and release a ROCm-enabled vLLM serving runtime image through the platform build pipeline, pinning an upstream ROCm base image release.
- Define the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime resources that deploy the ROCm vLLM runtime for the models cleared by the validation campaign.
- Validate that KServe InferenceServices deploying this runtime schedule and run correctly on AMD GPU nodes (KServe itself is expected to work unchanged — this is a validation of the integration, not a KServe code change).
- Record which models are supported (the cleared set) and which are explicitly unsupported.
- Release-train integration: ensure the pinned upstream ROCm image release aligns with the platform release cadence, or document the deviation and its support implications.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm serving runtime image builds successfully through the platform build pipeline (pipeline green).
- A ServingRuntime definition deploys cleared models on AMD GPU nodes via KServe InferenceServices, verified with a functional smoke test on physical AMD Instinct hardware.
- The runtime image is pinned to an upstream ROCm release whose cadence aligns with the platform release train, or the deviation is documented.
- The supported model list exactly matches the models cleared by the validation campaign; models that failed parity are explicitly listed as unsupported.
- The runtime is included in the platform release machinery for the targeted release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): this epic productizes the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models the validation campaign clears.

# PyTorch ROCm training support (PyTorchJob)

## Description

This epic makes PyTorch training on ROCm a supported capability for single- and multi-GPU jobs submitted as PyTorchJobs. Workers run with ROCm-enabled PyTorch images and request `amd.com/gpu` resources, on physical AMD Instinct nodes.

## Scope

- Support PyTorchJob worker pods running ROCm-enabled PyTorch training images.
- Ensure single-GPU and multi-GPU job topologies work on AMD Instinct nodes, with `amd.com/gpu` resource requests in worker pod specs.
- Validate training jobs end-to-end on the provisioned AMD environment, including admission through Kueue with `amd.com/gpu` quota (the quota configuration itself is tracked separately under the Distributed Workloads component).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm-enabled PyTorch image runs to completion on an AMD Instinct node with `amd.com/gpu` allocated.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob runs to completion across multiple AMD GPUs with correct distributed-training behavior.
- Jobs are admitted through Kueue with `amd.com/gpu` quota handling (verified together with the Kueue quota work).
- Validation is executed on the provisioned AMD Instinct environment.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs; this epic delivers the Training Operator / PyTorchJob side of that requirement.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling

## Description

This epic delivers Kueue quota and admission support for the `amd.com/gpu` resource so that ROCm training jobs queue and are admitted correctly. Kueue is the platform's queueing system (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model with all-or-nothing admission); this work extends the quota model to AMD GPUs.

## Scope

- Define Kueue resource flavor(s) and ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota covering `amd.com/gpu`.
- Ensure PyTorchJobs requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted through Kueue with gang semantics (all-or-nothing via waitForPodsReady).
- Ensure jobs requesting more quota than available remain queued rather than partially scheduled.
- Validate quota enforcement and admission end-to-end with ROCm PyTorchJobs on the AMD environment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ClusterQueue quota limits for `amd.com/gpu` are enforced: jobs requesting more than the available quota are not admitted.
- PyTorchJobs requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted through Kueue with all-or-nothing semantics and run on AMD GPU nodes.
- When quota is exhausted, pending jobs queue and are admitted when quota frees up.
- Quota handling is validated together with the PyTorch ROCm training jobs on the provisioned AMD Instinct environment.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for jobs admitted through Kueue with `amd.com/gpu` quota handling; this epic delivers the Kueue quota/admission side of that requirement.
